why: The unique identifier for the campaign; use it to name files and to quote in any query.
Tells you which campaign is which and who to contact.
Grade structures vary between organisations; behaviours are pitched at the grade.

field: Where you applied (Civil Service Jobs, employer's site or email)
why: Applications made outside Civil Service Jobs cannot be tracked in your account.

field: Link to the advert and saved copy of the advert
why: Adverts come down after closing; you need them to prepare for interview.
Many adverts close at 23:55 (indicative); the advert's own closing time takes precedence.
Shows how long each stage is taking and when to follow up.

field: Success Profiles elements and behaviours assessed
why: Lets you match examples and feedback to what is being tested.

field: Version of CV, statement or examples submitted
why: Keep a copy of what you sent so you can reuse it and refer back to it if you are invited to interview.
Tests can usually be taken within a set number of days given in the invitation email.
A significant number of organisations use a 1 to 7 scale where a score of at least 4 is generally needed to progress.

field: Interview or assessment date, format and panel contact
why: Interviews usually last 30 to 60 minutes and may include a presentation.
Closes the loop and starts any feedback request.

field: Feedback requested, received and key points
why: Feedback helps you improve future applications.

field: Reserve list placement date and expiry
why: Reserve lists can be used for up to 12 months.

field: Provisional offer, pre-employment checks and formal offer dates
why: Checks can take several weeks; do not resign before a formal offer.

field: Your notice period and agreed start date
why: Your contract sets your notice; the statutory minimum is one week after a month's service.
Follow-up reminders keep each application moving.
